transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-05-19
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 mins
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE); Owen Park (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Meridian Head of ML); Raj Patel (CFO); Sophie Nguyen (Infra)

Summary:
High-level intake to understand Meridian's per-token cost sensitivity and decide between Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment for a customer-facing summarization product. Focus on batching/caching levers, expected QPS, budget caps, and security/residency constraints. Agreed to pilot hosted for benchmarking then reassess dedicated/private based on unit economics.

Topics: cost per token, batching impact, KV cache reuse, residency/SOC2, pilot scope, timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, we'll run through where meridian is at and then peel into the unit economics, quick intros?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: yeah hi, lena here, i run the ml org. we'll be evaluating an LLM-based summarization in customer support flows.
[00:16] Raj Patel: raj—cfo — looking to understand spend runway and if this will need capital commitments.
[00:21] Sophie Nguyen: sophie infra, i'll own networking and compliance pieces for private deploy.
[00:27] Owen Park: owen se at redwood, i can dig into batching and kv cache details.
[00:32] Maya Chen: awesome. agenda: quick stack + qps, cost targets, talk through hosted vs dedicated vs private, then pilot next steps.

[02:05] Lena: we're targeting 1.2k daily active users initially, about 10 requests per user a day, so roughly 12k requests/day. avg prompt length maybe 220 tokens in, 180 tokens out, so about 400 tokens per request.
[02:22] Owen: okay that maps to roughly 4.8M tokens/month. do you have a latency SLO? that will drive whether hosted with low-lat or dedicated pools is needed.
[02:35] Lena: we'd like 300–450ms p95 on simple summarization. sometimes longer on long docs is ok up to 800ms.
[02:42] Maya: good, so latency tight but not ultra-low. cost target from finance?
[02:48] Raj: we'd like to keep this under $10k/month initially. that includes tooling and egress — we're flexible but need predictability.

[05:10] Owen: big levers you'll see: batching, prefix / KV cache reuse for repeat context, model size & quantization. For example, with continuous batching you can reduce per-token GPU time by 20–40% depending on seq length distribution.
[05:33] Lena: can you walk through numbers — hosted per-token vs dedicated reserved cost?
[05:40] Maya: sure, rough numbers in the deck — hosted list approx $0.0008 - $0.0014 per token for generation on the models we recommend, embeddings different. Dedicated committed capacity can push effective marginal per-token to $0.00035 - $0.0006 depending on utilization and batch efficiency.
[05:58] Raj: so dedicated is like half the cost but needs commitment — what's the commit size and term?
[06:06] Maya: typical reserved capacity starts at monthly commitments for X GPUs or token volume; we do 12 or 36 month options for best rates. we can do pilot-friendly short bursts or trial credits to validate before committing.

[08:20] Sophie: for private/VPC, what's the delta in ops overhead? we need KMS/HSM integrations and audit logs for compliance.
[08:30] Owen: private deploy adds management overhead; runtime is the same but you host in your VPC or appliance. per-token cost will be similar to dedicated if you amortize hardware, but there's infra+support licensing that usually shifts up the fixed cost.
[08:44] Lena: any constraints on KV cache residency, e.g., can we keep cache in our infra for private?
[08:50] Owen: yes, private can keep KV and prefix caches local. hosted keeps cache in Redwood's fast storage but we provide controls for TTLs and redaction; for regulated workloads we recommend private.

[11:00] Raj: what about fallback behavior—if dedicated is saturated do we automatically spill to hosted cheaper models?
[11:12] Maya: yes we support smart routing and fallbacks. policy can be set: route to lower-cost model variant or degrade gracefully to cached responses.
[11:22] Raj: important to avoid cost spikes.

[14:00] Lena: you mentioned batching gains. in practice how do we estimate batch size gains given our average of 400 tokens per request and qps profile?
[14:10] Owen: with your profile (12k/day, spiky during support hours), if we configure continuous batching with a 25ms aggregation window and target batch sizes ~8–16, you'll see better GPU utilization. for medium models, that often reduces per-token compute ~25%. but cold starts and strict latency windows can reduce gains.
[14:35] Sophie: i worry about latency variance with batching. we can't have long tail for customer-facing chat.
[14:42] Owen: you can set latency SLOs and Redwood will trade batch windows vs latency. also KV cache reduces work by reusing past computations for shared context, further reducing tokens sent to model.

[20:00] Maya: for a pilot we usually recommend hosted so we can instrument actual token counts and show the delta with batching and cache turned on. then we model a dedicated projection.
[20:12] Lena: ok, hosted pilot — what's the expected timeline?
[20:18] Maya: we can stand up a pilot next week, run for 1–2 weeks. Owen will help with instrumentation and we'll return sample per-token breakdowns.

[25:00] Raj: can you give an example cost projection? say 4.8M tokens/month.
[25:08] Owen: hosted at $0.0011 per token ~ $5.3k/month. that's generation only ballpark; add embeddings or other ops. With batching+cache on hosted you could cut that by ~30% to ~$3.7k.
[25:25] Maya: dedicated projection — with reserved capacity and expected utilization, same volume could be ~$1.6k–$2.8k/month effective marginal cost, plus reserved monthly fee. numbers depend on utilization and term.
[25:40] Raj: that's promising. we want to ensure that the headroom for growth doesn't blow the budget—what's the rollover or burst cost?
[25:47] Maya: we provide burst capacity at higher marginal rates; routing policies can prevent unbounded bursts. we'll model a 20% burst scenario in the pricing sheet.

[31:45] Sophie: security checklist — SSO/SAML, RBAC, audit logs, data residency. do you have SOC2 and encryption support?
[31:53] Maya: yes SOC2 Type II, SAML, RBAC, audit logs surface in Redwood Console, KMS integrations available both for Dedicated and Private. we'll send security pack.
[32:08] Lena: any red flags for PII — we need to redact customer PII before sending to hosted endpoints.
[32:15] Owen: you can do client-side redaction or use our redaction hooks; also private keeps data on-prem.

[40:00] (cross talk)
[40:12] Raj: competitor question — could we just use OpenAI and manage caching ourselves?
[40:20] Maya: you could, but Redwood's differentiation is the serving runtime and out-of-the-box batching/caching and routing that saves dev time and unit cost. plus the dedicated/private options with SLA and enterprise controls.
[40:33] Lena: also we like the per-route cost visibility; that's been a pain point for us internally.

[46:10] Owen: quick technical note — we instrument per-token GPU time and provide a KV cache hit rate dashboard. if you send a representative prompt set we can estimate expected hit rates and show projected savings.
[46:22] Lena: we'll share a prompt set — maybe 200 typical tickets.
[46:28] Owen: perfect, with that we'll run a simulated run in the sandbox and return a modeled projection.

[55:00] Recap and next steps
[55:05] Maya: recap: run hosted pilot for 1–2 weeks; get prompt set and QPS profile; we'll send pricing sheet and security docs; Owen compiles benchmarking notes. decision timeline: meridian aims to decide pilot go/no-go by 2026-05-28.
[55:25] Lena: sounds good.
[55:29] Raj: will review with finance; we want a conservative runway for month 1.
[55:33] Sophie: i'll follow up on network/VPC questions if we go private.

[61:00] End of call
